subject: Closing playbook: node affirmation & capacity commit pathway
messages:
From: Ethan Liao <ethan.liao@nimbusone.ai>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement - NimbusOne <procurement@nimbusone.ai>
Date: Mon, 17 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated sizing ask + hold request for late-stage procurement

Grace —

Thanks for the call this morning. We are in final procurement reviews and need a short, written affirmation of node availability to show the board. High level ask: can Redwood provision a dedicated pool for NimbusOne with roughly 24 A100-equivalent GPUs starting mid-Oct (week of 10/12), with the ability to scale to 40 GPUs by November? We understand this is aggressive; at minimum we need a firm reservation for 18 GPUs and a 30-day soft hold option for the rest while we close contracts.

Can you confirm what you can firmly commit to today and whether Redwood can place a 30d soft-hold on an additional buffer? We attached the Q4 ask spreadsheet for context.

Also, procurement will need a short note for our contract packet that describes Redwood's hold procedure and rollback policy.

Appreciate a quick turnaround — the board meeting is next Tuesday (8/24).

Thanks,
Ethan Liao
CTO, NimbusOne
Attachment: nimbusone_q4_asks.xlsx
From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Ethan Liao <ethan.liao@nimbusone.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 17 Aug 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated sizing ask + hold request for late-stage procurement

Ethan —

Thanks for the spreadsheet and the timeline. I looped in Ben (capacity/ops) and Karthik (sales ops) to validate inventory and propose the hold mechanics. High level we can provide a written affirmation for the firm portion and a documented 30-day soft-hold for the buffer while you close.

Next steps I propose:
- Ben: can you validate availability and give us a node map (firm vs buffer)
- Karthik: please draft the short hold procedure language for procurement and attach to this thread
- Ethan: if you can share the high-level SLA expectations (p99 latency, support hours) we can align the commit with the right Dedicated tier

I attached a one-pager summarizing the commitment language we typically provide for late-stage deals. If Ops can confirm by EOD tomorrow we can send NimbusOne a signed affirmation for the 18-node firm commit and outline the 30-day buffer.

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Account Executive — Strategic
Redwood Inference
Attachment: deal-summary-onepager.pdf
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 17 Aug 2026 15:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated sizing ask + hold request for late-stage procurement

Grace / Karthik —

Ops run the availability check this afternoon. Short summary below (all numbers expressed in A100-equivalent GPUs):

- Immediate firm availability (Q4 week of 10/12 start): 18 GPUs (3 x 6-GPU pods) that can be reserved today. These are in our US-west Dedicated pool and can be pinned to a customer tenant.
- Buffer capacity (soft-hold candidate): additional 12 GPUs spread across two pods (6 + 6) that we can earmark as a 30-day soft-hold. Buffer is not physically allocated but will be the first to be provisioned if not consumed by other queued workloads.
- Risk notes: 1) If commitments materialize across other Q4 deals, we may need to split buffer pods across AZs which could add ~10-12% provisioning latency. 2) Quantization/partitioning may be necessary if you need >40 effective GPUs immediately; we recommend the progressive ramp plan in the attached matrix.

Recommendation: Affirm 18 GPUs as firm commit under Deal NIM-4391, and attach a 30-day soft-hold on the 12-GPU buffer. Ops will raise a capacity hold ticket and flag the pods in the console; we'll also publish a rollback clause that releases the buffer automatically at the end of the hold window if unused.

Attachment: capacity-matrix-20260817.csv

Ben Carter
Head of Capacity Planning
Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated sizing ask + hold request for late-stage procurement

Thanks Ben — this alignment looks right. Grace, please send the written affirmation to NimbusOne with the following bullets in the packet:

- Firm commit: 18 A100-equivalent GPUs for Deal NIM-4391, start window week of 10/12/2026.
- Soft-hold: 12 GPUs reserved as a 30-day soft-hold (hold start date to be negotiated with customer) — buffer will be released automatically if not consumed within the window.
- Provisioning notes: pods flagged in US-west; potential AZ split risk and expected provisioning delta documented.
- SLA & escalation: reference Dedicated Tier 2 support, p99 latency targets, and a single point of contact from CSOps for the ramp.

I'll open CAP-4821 in Jira to capture the hold and routing rules and mark finance for a potential deferment on invoicing until ramp triggers. Marissa — loop in legal if Procurement asks for any language changes, but this is standard.

Grace — when you send to NimbusOne please copy me. Once we have NimbusOne sign-off, Ops will promote the hold to an enforced reservation.

Karthik Iyer
Sales Operations
Redwood Inference
